claims.text: Governor Kathy Hochul's Executive Order No. 65, effective 5 October 2026 for the entire State of New York and in effect until 4 November 2026, declares a State Disaster Emergency in response to the growing number of measles cases across rural areas of New York; the accompanying press release reports 108 confirmed cases in New York State in 2026 as of 3 October (7 in New York City, 101 in the rest of the state), 92 of them reported since 15 July 2026 among under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties, and states local health departments have administered over 1,000 doses of the MMR vaccine in rural areas of the state.

CDC's measles data page states: "As of November 5, 2026, 5,182 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026," up from 4,852 as of 29 October; the cumulative "Total Deaths" figure holds at 4, footnoted as subject to change.

CDC's measles data page (fetched 13 November 2026) reports 5,182 confirmed US measles cases, "As of November 5, 2026" (unchanged), and now lists the cumulative 2026 US death toll at 6, up from 4, with a footnote: "This number is subject to change; CDC will update its reporting as additional information becomes available and relevant reviews are completed."
CDC's measles data page reports 4,080 confirmed measles cases in the United States in 2026 as of 8 October 2026, up from 3,887 as of 1 October, with a cumulative total of 2 US measles deaths.

CDC's measles data page states: "As of October 15, 2026, 4,410 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026," up from 4,080 as of October 8, with a cumulative total of 2 US measles deaths (a figure the page notes is subject to change).

CDC's measles data page, checked 21 October 2026, still states "As of October 15, 2026, 4,410 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026," but now lists a cumulative "Total Deaths" figure of 3 (footnoted "This number is subject to change; CDC will update its reporting"), up from the 2 shown on the same page as of 19 October 2026 for the same October 15 data cut.

CDC's measles data page, checked 23 October 2026, states 4,588 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026 as of 12:00PM on 22 October, up from 4,410 as of 15 October; the cumulative 'Total Deaths' figure remains 3, footnoted as subject to change.

CDC's measles data page, checked 31 October 2026, states 4,852 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026 as of 29 October 2026, up from 4,588 as of 22 October; the cumulative 'Total Deaths' figure remains 3, footnoted as subject to change.

Governor Kathy Hochul statement, 2 November 2026: "I am heartbroken to learn that a child in Lewis County has died after contracting measles." The statement calls it New York State's first measles-related death in 30 years and urges vaccination as the best protection against the disease.

Executive Order No. 65.1 (signed 4 November 2026) extends the State Disaster Emergency first declared in Executive Order No. 65, citing that "the number of measles cases reported this year has markedly increased," and additionally authorizes licensed but unregistered retired physicians, nurses and nurse practitioners to join state or local measles immunization efforts. "This executive order shall be in effect through December 4, 2026."

CDC's measles data page, checked 5 November 2026, states 4,852 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026 as of October 29, 2026 (unchanged from the prior check), but the cumulative "Total Deaths" figure for the same data cut has risen to 4, up from 3, a figure the page continues to flag as subject to change.

description: Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on 5 October 2026 over a measles outbreak concentrated in under-immunized rural communities. On 2 November, Hochul announced that a child in Lewis County had died after contracting measles — New York State's first measles-related death in 30 years — and on 4 November she signed Executive Order No. 65.1 extending the disaster emergency through 4 December 2026, citing a continued rise in cases. As of 3 October, New York had recorded 108 confirmed cases in 2026 (7 in New York City, 101 elsewhere), 92 of them since 15 July across 18 rural counties. The New York outbreak is part of a wider US measles resurgence: CDC's dashboard shows 5,182 confirmed cases nationwide as of 5 November 2026, with the cumulative national death toll now at 6, up from 4, a figure CDC flags as subject to change.

impact.summary: Governor Hochul announced on 2 November 2026 that a child in Lewis County died after contracting measles, New York State's first measles-related death in 30 years, and on 4 November she signed Executive Order No. 65.1 extending the state's measles disaster emergency through 4 December 2026. As of 3 October 2026, New York had recorded 108 confirmed measles cases in 2026 (7 in New York City, 101 elsewhere), 92 of them since 15 July concentrated in under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties; local health departments have administered over 1,000 MMR doses in response. Nationally, CDC's dashboard shows 5,182 confirmed US measles cases as of 5 November 2026, and now lists the cumulative national death toll at 6 (up from 4), a figure CDC again flags as subject to change.
